stories.headline: US holds off on planned Iran strikes amid talks on nuclear deal and shipping routes
stories.body:
United States President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social on Saturday that he cancelled planned military strikes against Iran [c1]. He stated that calling off the attacks was contingent on rapidly reaching a deal regarding Iran's nuclear programme and reopening the Strait of Hormuz [c2].

However, Iranian officials and news outlets challenged the US narrative. The Iranian news agency Mehr stated on Sunday that Donald Trump's assertion that Tehran requested a pause on strikes was a lie [c3]. Iran's acting defence minister Majid Ebn-e-Reza posted on X that Iranian forces would remain on alert and would not be taken by surprise [c4]. In addition, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi informed Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan that any military attacks by the US or Israel would be met with a proportionate response [c15].

Despite the tense statements, diplomatic discussions appear to be making progress through regional mediators. Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesperson for the Iranian parliament's national security commission, stated that mediators were attempting to revive a June agreement brokered by Pakistan [c5]. On Telegram, Foreign Minister Araghchi posted that negotiations between Tehran and Muscat over the Strait of Hormuz are entering their final stages [c8]. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei also stated that Iran and Oman were close to an understanding on a new maritime route through the Strait of Hormuz [c9]. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian posted on X that a memorandum of understanding with the US would become the cornerstone of Tehran's foreign relations [c12]. Regional leaders have also engaged directly; Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Donald Trump by phone on Saturday to urge de-escalation regarding Iran [c6].

The sudden shift follows recent military actions and caught key allies unawares. On February 28, the US and Israel launched strikes aimed at destroying Iran's missile programme [c10]. Channel 12 reported that Israeli officials and US Central Command first learned of Donald Trump's decision to call off the new strikes via his Truth Social post [c14].

The situation remains critical for international trade. Approximately 20 percent of global oil consumption normally passes through the Strait of Hormuz [c11]. Maritime trade tracking firm Kpler reported on Friday that vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz had dropped sharply [c13].

Meanwhile, conflict persists across the wider region. Israeli airstrikes on Gaza on Sunday killed at least 18 Palestinians across Gaza City, Deir al-Balah, and Khan Younis [c7].

stories.headline: Two dead in helicopter collision during wildfire firefighting efforts in Greece
stories.body:
A mid-air collision between two leased Bell helicopters during firefighting operations in Greece killed a Danish pilot and a Greek fire service liaison officer on Sunday [c16]. A British pilot and a Greek coordinator survived the crash, which occurred near the Attica-Boeotia border [c17] during water-dropping operations near Psatha in western Attica [c25].

Following the fatal accident, authorities grounded all Bell helicopters across Greece [c18]. Both aircraft involved had been leased from Australia's McDermott Aviation [c21]. Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis expressed his deepest sorrow on X over the loss of the Greek coordinator and Danish pilot [c19].

The collision took place as over 500 firefighters fought blazes for 72 hours across regions including Porto Germeno, Psatha, Fokida, Megara, and Kefalonia [c20]. More than 100 homes were destroyed overnight around the coastal village of Porto Germeno, located about 45 miles northwest of Athens [c22]. A new wildfire also broke out overnight on the Ionian island of Kefalonia, prompting evacuations in the Pastra area [c26]. These events follow the deaths of three Greek firefighters last week from injuries sustained battling wildfires [c23]. Elsewhere, a mega-fire in Gironde, France, was contained after forcing the evacuation of 224,000 people [c24].

stories.headline: Bomb blast outside Moscow restaurant leaves at least three dead and dozens injured
stories.body:
A bomb explosion outside an Italian restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square in central Moscow killed at least three people on Saturday [c27, c28, c30]. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin described the blast, which occurred around 20:00 local time, as a brutal terrorist act [c27, c30].

Russian state media reported that the explosion took place at the entrance of the Balzi Rossi restaurant, located inside a Stalin-era skyscraper, killing a security guard, a restaurant guest, and the female bomber [c28, c33]. The National Anti-Terrorism Committee stated that at least 21 people were injured [c29]. Later, REN TV reported that two hospitalized victims died on Sunday, raising the unconfirmed death toll to five [c32]. Sergey Goncharov, a veteran of Russia's Alpha counter-terrorism unit, suggested the female carrier might have been an unwitting courier delivered money to carry the package [c31].

In separate military actions over the weekend, a Ukrainian drone attack on an apartment block in Engels, Russia, killed two people [c34]. Russia's Defense Ministry stated that Ukrainian drones also struck a Wildberries warehouse in the Samara Oblast [c35].

vocab.meaning: not done on purpose or without awareness of the full situation

stories.headline: Massive migrant crossing in Ceuta triggers political fallout across Europe
stories.body:
A major surge of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta has sparked political reactions across Europe [c36, c40, c45]. Around 60,000 migrants crossed the border from Morocco into Ceuta over several days starting Thursday [c40].

The surge resulted in tragic loss of life. At least 72 people died attempting to cross into Ceuta, drowning or being crushed near the border fence [c38]. Morocco's Interior Ministry reported 11 deaths, mostly from drowning [c41], while Ceuta leader Juan Jesus Vivas stated the city's morgue received 88 corpses, including victims from earlier crossing attempts [c42]. On Saturday, Spanish police installed a 500-metre floating barrier off the border [c39]. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez assured British Prime Minister Andy Burnham that roughly 98% of the estimated 50,000 migrants who entered Ceuta had been returned to Morocco [c37]. Burnham pledged to be relentless in tackling small boat Channel crossings following the crisis [c36].

Political tension heightened in response to the crisis. Far-right European Parliament member Alvise Pérez was confronted by counterprotesters in Ceuta on Saturday and sheltered inside a bar until police intervened [c43]. On Sunday, Vox party leader Santiago Abascal visited Ceuta and criticized the government, labeling the influx an invasion [c44]. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni suspended Italy's Schengen agreement with Spain, citing security concerns [c45].

vocab.meaning: a portion of territory surrounded by a larger territory whose inhabitants are culturally or ethnically distinct
an arrival or entry of large numbers of people or things

stories.headline: Suicide bombing at peace rally in Pakistan's Swat district kills 14
stories.body:
A suicide attack outside a police station in Kabal, located in Pakistan's Swat district, killed at least 14 people and injured more than two dozen on Sunday [c46]. Demonstrators had gathered near the police station for the Olasi Pasoon peace gathering to demand an end to militant violence in the Swat Valley [c47, c53]. District police chief Omar Khan stated that the bomber detonated explosives while demonstrators were chanting anti-militant slogans [c47].

Authorities confirmed that nine civilians and five police officers were among those killed [c48]. Swat Deputy Inspector General of Police Fida Hussain reported that at least 22 people were wounded in the explosion [c50]. The bombing follows an attack three days prior, in which an ambush using explosive-laden drones killed 11 police officers at a checkpoint in Hangu district [c51].

The deadly bombing reflects a wider wave of violence in the region. Military spokesperson Ahmad Sharif Chaudhry stated that Pakistan has recorded 3,145 terrorism-related incidents since January, resulting in 819 security and civilian deaths [c49]. Furthermore, the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies recorded 154 terrorism-related deaths across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in July [c52].

stories.headline: Heavy monsoon rains and landslides in Kerala leave eight dead and eight missing
stories.body:
Torrential monsoon rains and multiple landslides across Kerala have resulted in significant casualties and destruction [c54, c56]. Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan confirmed that eight people died, eight remain missing, and 13 were injured following the severe weather [c54].

The India Meteorological Department issued an orange alert for 12 districts in Kerala on Sunday, warning residents of potential flash floods and mudslides [c55]. Rain measurements showed extreme levels in several areas. Peerumade and Thodupuzha taluks in Idukki received over 200 mm of rainfall on Saturday morning, which triggered multiple landslides [c56]. The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority recorded the highest rainfall of 320 mm at Ayyankunnu in Kannur district on Saturday [c57].

The deluge caused severe local accidents and stream overflows. In Malappuram, three-year-old Abdul Muhaini and four-year-old Adam Ayman drowned after falling into a swollen stream [c59]. In response to the dangerous conditions, educational institutions in Pathanamthitta, Wayanad, Kannur, and Kasaragod districts were declared closed on August 3 [c58].

Heavy rainfall and flooding extended beyond Kerala into neighboring regions. In Gujarat's Vadodara district, rescue teams evacuated around 150 people, including 140 students, from a flooded hostel near Waghodia [c60].

vocab.meaning: an administrative subdivision of a district in India
a seasonal prevailing wind bringing heavy rainfall to South Asia

stories.headline: Slipper thrown at Independent MP Pappu Yadav during Delhi press conference
stories.body:
A political altercation occurred in Delhi after a man hurled a slipper at Independent MP Pappu Yadav during a press conference at his residence on Sunday evening around 6:15 p.m. [c61]. Delhi police took into custody a man identified as Sumit from Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh [c62]. Police questioned Sumit, a 34-year-old iron fabrication business owner from Ghaziabad [c65].

Pappu Yadav stated he was addressing questions regarding missing gold and silver following a skit on Ram Temple donation theft staged in Parliament on July 31 [c63]. Following complaints by seers regarding the skit, Varanasi police registered an FIR against Pappu Yadav, Rahul Gandhi, and Awadhesh Prasad [c64].

During the incident, Pappu Yadav's media convenor alleged that an attacker drew a knife [c67]. The event sparked political fallout, with Congress media head Pawan Khera criticizing Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and the police force for failing to protect Pappu Yadav at his residence [c66].

vocab.meaning: a noisy argument or disagreement in public
a person who arranges meetings or acts on behalf of a committee or group

stories.headline: Students in Jharkhand protest competitive exam irregularities with sit-in and rally
stories.body:
Hundreds of students staged an indefinite sit-in at Jaipal Singh Munda stadium in Ranchi for a fifth consecutive day on Sunday to protest competitive exam irregularities [c68]. On Sunday evening, the protesting students conducted a torchlight procession from the stadium to Albert Ekka Chowk in Ranchi [c69].

The protesters are demanding a CBI probe into all recruitment exams held by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) over the last seven years [c70]. They are also demanding the cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test held on April 19 [c70].

The demonstrations generated broader political support and dramatic incidents. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke posted on X extending support to the protesting students [c71]. On Sunday morning, a 25-year-old man named Heeralal climbed a 100-foot mobile tower at the stadium before being rescued by police [c72]. Meanwhile, the BJYM and BJP held demonstrations across East Singhbhum, West Singhbhum, and Chatra demanding a CBI investigation into JPSC and JSSC exam irregularities [c73].

vocab.meaning: an act or practice that fails to conform to official rules or standard procedure
denoting an action or event done in preparation for a main event

stories.headline: Cauvery water release triggers political disputes between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
stories.body:
Karnataka began releasing Cauvery water from the Kabini Dam on Saturday, raising discharge from 500 cusecs to 25,000 cusecs by Saturday night [c74]. The release follows a directive from the Cauvery Water Management Authority ordering Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days [c77].

The water dispute comes amidst low water levels and poor rainfall. On Sunday, the water level at Mettur Dam stood at 73.33 feet against its full capacity of 120 feet [c75]. Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar stated that Karnataka has received only about 35 percent of its normal rainfall so far this year [c78].

Political developments continue to unfold over the water sharing issue. D.K. Shivakumar stated that Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay agreed to postpone his planned visit to Bengaluru regarding the Cauvery dispute [c76]. However, Kannada Chaluvali leader Vatal Nagaraj stated that a proposed state-wide bandh in Karnataka will proceed on August 13 despite government appeals to withdraw it [c79]. In Tamil Nadu, BJP state president Nainar Nagenthran accused the Congress party of cheating Tamil Nadu farmers whenever it comes to power in Karnataka [c80].

vocab.meaning: a unit of flow rate equal to one cubic foot per second
a general strike or protest shutdown organized by a political group in India
